o1.biggest_strength: A dated calendar with owners that fits the 1 December freeze, six clear go/no-go gates, and channels ranked by retained users with the math shown.
o1.biggest_mistake: Extension authors are ranked #2 even though X kept more users (3,740 vs 2,470) and the reason isn't given; the 6,980–9,240 projection range is also muddled.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add engineering hours to the launch-week support rota and explain why authors rank above X despite X keeping more users.

o2.biggest_strength: Strong migration gates: a 1,000-user real-setup beta, one-step undo, top-200 extension testing, and engineers freed by the freeze joining daily support shifts.
o2.biggest_mistake: No owner per task, creators get the build only two weeks before launch, and the X thread and email are full of [placeholders], so the drafts aren't finished.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name an owner for every row, get creators the build earlier, and fill in the author credits and copy so the drafts are ready to paste.

reason: Both get the core right: retention over installs, migration as a launch gate, and the community first. Output 1 is the one I could hand my small team tomorrow, with owners, targets, a plan B and finished copy. Output 2 has smarter support ideas but leaves too many blanks.
